messages.subject: INLA mesh assessment
parts:
Hi, I have created my mesh using the code  below. the epsgKM function is a just a function of converting the crs to km.

```
kenya_shp1 <- as(as(st_transform(kenya_shapefile, epsgKM(32737)), 'Spatial'), 'SpatialPolygonsDataFrame')
coords_mesh = st_coordinates(clust.shp2)
kenya_shp <- fortify(kenya_shp1)
bdry <- inla.sp2segment(kenya_shp1)
shp.bnd <- cbind(kenya_shp$long, kenya_shp$lat)
c.bnd <- as.matrix(shp.bnd)

mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(
  boundary = bdry,
  loc = coords_mesh,
  loc.domain = c.bnd,
  max.edge = c(20, 40),
  cutoff = 1
)
``
The plot of the mesh produced is shown below. Afterwards, I assessed the mesh using the inla.mesh.assessment as shown below;
```
inla.mesh.assessment(mesh, spatial.range = 1, alpha = 2)

names       :                 sd,                                sd.dev,                      edge.len
min values  : 0.0226924990912104, 0.932960535274713, 0.871364819091162
max values  :  0.804490720522512,  1.09395249580249,   37.481814141564 
```
And from that, I can see that the std.dev ranges from  0.93 to 1.09, and the its plot is attached below. Can I confidently say that this a good mesh fit for my data?

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA mesh assessment
parts:
Hi,

since you assessed the approximation using a range much smaller than the max.edge setting for the mesh, I don't think the assessment plot says anything conclusive.
It's meant for the case when the range is _larger_ than the triangles.

Finn
```
